title: GitHub - palamim/starboard: A terminal that's always beside your Dock — not a Quake-style hotkey overlay, a permanent fixture
excerpt: A terminal that's always beside your Dock — not a Quake-style hotkey overlay, a permanent fixture - palamim/starboard
content_html:
A terminal that's just always there — not summoned, not dismissed.

Starboard lives permanently beside your macOS Dock: on screen, on every desktop, all the time. There's no hotkey to call it up and no window to find, resize, or alt-tab back to, because it never goes away in the first place.

How this differs from Quake-style terminals

Guake, Yakuake, tilda, iTerm2's hotkey window, Ghostty's quick terminal — these summon a terminal with a hotkey, hand it focus, and dismiss it again when you're done. Same family, different interaction model: Starboard has no hotkey, never takes focus, and has no summon/dismiss cycle. It's not called up — it's just sitting there, the way the Dock itself is.

That's the point of it: moving between desktops running a command in whatever project directory you're in, then going straight back to the editor — without switching to a terminal app, waiting on a window animation, or losing your place when you switch back.

What it does

  • Sits directly beside the Dock, tracking its height and position live.
  • Visible on every Space, including over full-screen apps — never steals focus from whatever app you're in.
  • A real, persistent shell (zsh -l): cd, history, and state carry over between commands, same as any terminal tab — not a one-shot command runner.
  • Its own dark look and a muted, nautical ANSI color palette — not a system lookalike.
  • Cmd+E expands it to full screen height (growing upward from the Dock) when you need more room — long output, or running something like Claude Code in there — then Cmd+E again to snap back to Dock height.

Requirements

  • macOS 13+
  • Accessibility permission (prompted on first launch) — used to read the Dock's live position. Starboard still works without it, just pinned to a fixed corner instead of hugging the Dock.
  • Currently assumes a bottom-docked Dock on the main display. Left/right Dock placement and multi-monitor setups aren't handled yet — feedback and contributions welcome.

Security & trust

Starboard makes no network requests and collects no data — there's nothing in the source that could, since it's under 700 lines across 4 Swift files, worth reading yourself rather than taking on faith. The one sensitive-looking permission it asks for, Accessibility, is used for exactly one thing: reading the Dock's on-screen position so the panel can sit next to it. scripts/install.sh only touches your own user-level LaunchAgents and login keychain (never system-wide, never sudo), and the local code-signing certificate it creates is scoped narrowly to code signing — it exists purely so macOS remembers the Accessibility grant across rebuilds, not for anything else.

Download

Grab the latest build from Releases, then:

unzip Starboard.zip
mv Starboard.app /Applications/
open /Applications/Starboard.app

The build is ad-hoc signed, not notarized (notarization needs a paid Apple Developer account), so the first launch takes a few more clicks than a notarized app would:

  1. Opening it is blocked outright ("Starboard" Not Opened) — click Done.
  2. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down, and click Open Anyway next to the Starboard entry.
  3. A second confirmation dialog appears ("Open Starboard?") — click Open Anyway again, then enter your password when prompted.
  4. Starboard launches, but won't be glued to the Dock yet — a separate Accessibility Access prompt appears. Click Open System Settings and enable Starboard under Privacy & Security → Accessibility.

If you already have Starboard installed via scripts/install.sh, you'll see two "Starboard" entries in that Accessibility list — one per build, since each is signed differently (see below). They can be hard to tell apart, and enabling the new one doesn't always seem to take by itself — if it's still not tracking the Dock, remove the older entry (select it, click −) and re-enable the remaining one.

If you'd rather not click through all of that, the source is under 700 lines across 4 Swift files — worth reading, and buildable yourself with swift build below instead.

Each release is signed ad-hoc, and that signature differs between builds, so updating to a new version may ask you to re-grant Accessibility permission (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility) even if you'd already granted it for the previous one.

Build from source

Run it once:

swift build
.build/debug/Starboard

Run at login (packages and code-signs a .app, registers it as a LaunchAgent):

scripts/install.sh

Stop / start / remove:

launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.starboard.app.plist   # stop
launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.starboard.app.plist     # start
scripts/uninstall.sh                                              # remove entirely

Logs: ~/Library/Logs/Starboard.log

Known issues

  • Pasted text briefly renders in the wrong color until the next keypress.
  • (Previously) some prompt glyphs rendered as ? during live redraws — hasn't recurred recently.

See CLAUDE.md for architecture, design decisions, and the full write-up on both issues above.

License

MIT — see LICENSE.

content_html_zh:
一个始终存在的终端——不会被召唤，也不会被解雇。

Starboard 永久位于 macOS Dock 旁边：始终在屏幕上、每个桌面上。 没有热键可以调用它，也没有窗口可以查找、调整大小或使用 alt-tab 返回，因为它从一开始就永远不会消失。

这与 Quake 风格的终端有何不同

Guake、Yakuake、tilda、iTerm2 的热键窗口、Ghostty 的快速终端 - 这些都会用热键召唤一个终端，将焦点移交给它，然后在完成后再次关闭它。 相同的家族，不同的交互模式：右舷没有热键，从不获取焦点，并且没有召唤/解散周期。 它没有被调用——它只是坐在那里，就像 Dock 本身一样。

这就是它的要点：在桌面之间移动，在您所在的任何项目目录中运行命令，然后直接返回编辑器 - 无需切换到终端应用程序，等待窗口动画，也无需在切换回来时丢失位置。

它的作用

  • 直接坐在码头旁边，实时跟踪其高度和位置。
  • 在每个空间上都可见，包括在全屏应用程序上 - 永远不会从您所在的任何应用程序中夺走焦点。
  • 真实、持久的 shell (zsh -l)：cd、历史记录和状态在命令之间传递，与任何终端选项卡相同 — 不是一次性命令运行程序。
  • 它自己的深色外观和柔和的航海 ANSI 调色板——与系统不同。
  • 当您需要更多空间（长输出，或在其中运行类似 Claude Code 的内容）时，Cmd+E 将其扩展到全屏高度（从 Dock 向上增长），然后再次 Cmd+E 快速恢复到 Dock 高度。

要求

  • macOS 13+
  • 辅助功能权限（首次启动时提示）- 用于读取 Dock 的实时位置。 右舷在没有它的情况下仍然可以工作，只是固定在固定的角落而不是紧贴码头。
  • 目前假定主显示屏上有一个底部停靠的 Dock。 左/右 Dock 放置和多显示器设置尚未处理 - 欢迎反馈和贡献。

安全与信任

Starboard 不发出任何网络请求，也不收集任何数据——源代码中没有任何内容可以做到这一点，因为它的 4 个 Swift 文件不到 700 行，值得你自己阅读而不是相信。 它要求的一项看似敏感的权限“辅助功能”仅用于一件事：读取 Dock 在屏幕上的位置，以便面板可以位于它旁边。 scripts/install.sh 只涉及您自己的用户级 LaunchAgents 和登录钥匙串（绝不是系统范围的，绝不是 sudo），并且它创建的本地代码签名证书的范围仅限于代码签名 - 它的存在纯粹是为了 macOS 记住重建期间的辅助功能授予，而不是其他任何东西。

下载

从发布中获取最新版本，然后：

unzip Starboard.zip
mv Starboard.app /Applications/
open /Applications/Starboard.app

该构建是临时签名的，未经过公证（公证需要付费的 Apple 开发者帐户），因此首次启动比经过公证的应用程序需要更多的点击次数：

  1. 打开它被完全阻止（“右舷”未打开）- 单击“完成”。
  2. 打开“系统设置”→“隐私和安全”，向下滚动，然后单击“右舷”条目旁边的“仍然打开”。
  3. 出现第二个确认对话框（“打开右舷？”） - 再次单击“仍然打开”，然后在出现提示时输入密码。
  4. Starboard 启动，但还不会粘在 Dock 上 - 会出现一个单独的辅助功能访问提示。 单击“打开系统设置”并在“隐私和安全”→“辅助功能”下启用 Starboard。

如果您已经通过 script/install.sh 安装了 Starboard，您将在该辅助功能列表中看到两个“Starboard”条目 - 每个版本一个，因为每个条目的签名都不同（见下文）。 它们可能很难区分，并且启用新条目似乎并不总是自动完成 - 如果它仍然没有跟踪 Dock，请删除旧条目（选择它，单击 -）并重新启用其余条目。

如果您不想点击查看所有内容，源代码包含 4 个 Swift 文件，共 700 行——值得一读，并且可以使用下面的 swift build 自行构建。

每个版本都是临时签名的，并且该签名在构建之间有所不同，因此更新到新版本可能会要求您重新授予可访问性权限（系统设置→隐私和安全→可访问性），即使您已经为前一个版本授予了该权限。

从源代码构建

运行一次：

swift build
.build/debug/Starboard

登录时运行（对 .app 进行打包和代码签名，将其注册为 LaunchAgent）：

scripts/install.sh

停止/启动/删除：

launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.starboard.app.plist   # stop
launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.starboard.app.plist     # start
scripts/uninstall.sh                                              # remove entirely

日志：~/Library/Logs/Starboard.log
